topPRs.title: test: Super ZK Dispute Game Integration Test Coverage Improvements
topPRs.author: 0xarktos
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Adds 4 new integration test scenarios to `ZKDisputeGameIntegration.t.sol` to increase coverage around respected-type semantics, guardian blacklisting, parent/child propagation, and chain-set evolution:

- **Scenario 4** — A ZK game created while ZK is not the respected game type resolves to `DEFENDER_WINS` and enters `NORMAL` bond distribution, but `setAnchorState()` is silently skipped because `isGameRespected()` returns false. The proposer still claims the full bond back.
- **Scenario 5** — The guardian blacklists a challenged game before `closeGame()` runs. `isGameProper()` returns false → `REFUND` mode; both proposer and challenger reclaim their original deposits regardless of the `CHALLENGER_WINS` outcome.
- **Scenario 6** — A blacklisted parent does not automatically invalidate an in-flight child. The child resolves `DEFENDER_WINS`, enters `NORMAL` bond distribution, and the proposer reclaims the bond — the guardian must explicitly blacklist the child to invalidate it.
- **Scenario 7** — A child game can commit to a different chain set than its parent. Parent has 2 chains, child adds a third; `absolutePrestate` is rotated in the factory `gameArgs` between the two games to match the expected production flow. Both games are self-proved via `prove()`, resolve `DEFENDER_WINS`, and finalize. Per-chain lookups remain isolated to each game's committed chain set. In production this rotation would also require a new ZK program vkey.

## Test plan

- `DEV_FEATURE__ZK_DISPUTE_GAME=true forge test --match-path "test/dispute/zk/*"` — all tests pass

### Notes
- `just pr` throws false semver errors. Once the main contract changes are merged, this will be resolved since versions were correctly updated in the other PR.

topPRs.title: chore(reth-optimism c1): drop allows and fix warnings in trie/flashblocks/consensus/primitives/storage
topPRs.author: theochap
topPRs.body:
Part 1 of 3 refix passes on PR #20327.

Drops the crate-level `#![allow(clippy::...)]` blanket blocks in the 5
heavy data-layer crates and replaces them with either in-source fixes or
narrowly scoped per-file / per-item allows that document the
architectural reason. Also fixes a latent no-std build break introduced
by the parent branch in `reth-optimism-consensus`.

## Crates covered

- `reth-optimism-storage` — no warnings remain after dropping the block
- `reth-optimism-primitives` — literal separators, `OnceLock::new()`, targeted truncation allows for bit-flag casts
- `reth-optimism-consensus` — new `# Errors` sections, `#[must_use]` on builders, trailing-semicolons, tests get scoped allows for hex-heavy fixtures
- `reth-optimism-trie` — per-file allows reflecting mdbx tx drop guards, isize/usize nibble arithmetic, and the uniform `OpProofsStorageResult` trait surface
- `reth-optimism-flashblocks` — per-module allows with rationale, `#[must_use]` on builder methods, `# Errors` where succinct, `let…else` fix in the reconciliation strategy

## Notable fix

One commit (`fix(reth-optimism-consensus): use core-reachable Clone::clone path`) restores the no-std build of `reth-optimism-consensus`: commit 6e1bd77 on the parent branch replaced a `|r| r.clone()` closure with `std::clone::Clone::clone`, but the crate is declared `default-features = false` in the workspace and the `std` path is unresolved under `no_std`. Any transitive dependency chain that builds consensus without its default `std` feature (e.g. `reth-optimism-flashblocks` → `payload-builder` → `evm` → `consensus`) fails with E0433. Switching to the prelude-reachable `Clone::clone` resolves it.

## Verification

- `cargo clippy -p reth-optimism-{trie,flashblocks,consensus,primitives,storage} --all-targets --tests -- -W clippy::pedantic -W clippy::nursery --cap-lints warn` is clean
- `cargo test -p reth-optimism-{trie,flashblocks,consensus,primitives,storage} --tests` passes (138 tests)
- `cargo build -p reth-optimism-{trie,flashblocks,consensus,primitives,storage}` succeeds
- `cargo +nightly fmt` applied

## Test plan

- [ ] CI clippy passes with pedantic + nursery on the 5 crates
- [ ] Downstream crates (node, rpc, payload, evm, txpool) still compile and test

topPRs.title: feat(op-challenger): add game-proposal-outputs subcommand (replaces shell script)
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
> Draft — alternative to #21541. That PR fixes the shell script in place; this one ports it to a native subcommand instead, for comparison.

## What

Replaces `op-challenger/scripts/game-proposal-outputs.sh` with a native `op-challenger game-proposal-outputs` subcommand.

For each dispute game — enumerated from the factory within the game window, or the explicitly-named game addresses — it reports:
- `outputRoot`: what our op-node derives at the proposed L2 block, with `rootMatch` vs the on-chain proposal
- `safeHead`: our node's safe head at the game's `l1Head` anchor, with `safeHeadAtOrAboveBlock`

A root mismatch, or a safe head below the proposed block, means a challenger pointed at this node would dispute the proposal. Supports `--format text|json`.

## Why a subcommand

op-challenger already has the sibling debug tools (`list-games`, `list-claims`), the contract bindings (`l2BlockNumber()`/`l1Head()`/factory enumeration), and the rollup client wired up. The shell script reimplemented all of that by hand with `eth_call` + `python3`, which is how it ended up with a JSON serialization bug that made it silently non-functional (see #21541). The subcommand reuses the existing, tested plumbing.

## Test

- `go test ./op-challenger/cmd/` (new render tests for text + json, incl. omitted factory index for explicit-game form)
- Live against soneium-minato-sepolia op-node, both factory-enumeration and explicit-game forms:

```
Game                                       Status        L2 Block Output Root (ours)                                                 Match      L1 Head    Safe Head    Ok
0x3ddfB3C5EcB18fE5f4DcFfe052CbEC3c3853344e In Progress   29541759 0xede109637900d069eab8a7dfcced76725b303df0cb0feb4c1890903173c9da62  true     11127878     29542323  true
```

Updates the dispute-game investigation doc + agent/skill references to the subcommand.

topPRs.title: fix(op-interop-filter): accept same-timestamp executing messages
topPRs.author: damilolaedwards
topPRs.body:
**Description**

`validateMessageTiming` in op-interop-filter rejected an executing message whose
initiating message shared the same timestamp. Rule 1 used
`initTimestamp >= inclusionTimestamp`, but the canonical rule is `init <= inclusion`:
depset `CanExecute`, the supernode verifier, and the kona `MessageGraph` all accept
equality, and the spec treats same-timestamp (same-block) interop as valid. The strict
comparison caused the filter to reject valid messages and disagree with the fault-proof
system, which op-reth treats as a definitive-invalid verdict and drops the transaction.

This changes Rule 1 to reject only `initTimestamp > inclusionTimestamp`, so the filter
matches consensus. The error message is updated accordingly. The change is one operator
in `lockstep_cross_validator.go`.

**Tests**

- Added a differential fuzz (`timing_parity_fuzz_test.go`) comparing the filter timing
  rule against the real `depset.CanExecute` over 200,000 bounded random
  `(init, inclusion, expiryWindow)` tuples: 0 disagreements. Coverage is asserted
  non-vacuous (init == inclusion, off-by-one on each side, and the expiry boundary are
  each exercised tens of thousands of times, and both accept and reject verdicts occur).
- Added focused boundary tests: `init == inclusion` accepts, `init > inclusion` rejects,
  `init + window == inclusion` accepts (not expired), `init + window == inclusion - 1`
  rejects (expired).
- Added an end-to-end test that the real `ValidateAccessEntry` now returns nil for
  `init == inclusion` (previously it returned a conflict error).
- Updated the two existing tests that asserted the old strict behavior.
- Full `op-interop-filter/filter` package passes and `go vet` is clean.

**Additional context**

The filter was strictly more conservative than consensus (it rejected something valid
and never accepted something invalid), so the impact is liveness and divergence rather
than acceptance of invalid messages: valid same-block interop transactions were dropped
by filter-gated nodes, and those nodes disagreed with the fault-proof system. A deferred
executing message (inclusion timestamp strictly greater) was unaffected.

One intentional non-divergence remains outside the realistic input range: at the uint64
ceiling the filter rejects on `init + window` overflow (checked add) while depset uses a
saturating add. This is unreachable in practice since timestamps are seconds, so it is
excluded from the parity claim.
